Hi Tessa,

Thanks for agreeing to take a look at our identity controls requirements — we’re evaluating vendors for a new onboarding/workflow automation project and need detail on three areas:

- Zero-touch provisioning (IDP-initiated user creation + attribute mapping) and just-in-time access behavior
- SCIM v2 capabilities: bulk imports, delta token support, incremental sync, group membership semantics, and error handling
- RBAC / delegated admin model (tenant-scoped admins, limited-scope admin consoles, audit provenance)

I attached a short RFI spreadsheet (CoreLedger_RFI_20270712.xlsx) with the specific questions and the timeline we’re working to. Ideally we’d like capability summary docs and any supporting architecture diagrams by EOD Wednesday so our security team can triage. Can Redwood provide:

1) A capability pack describing SSO (SAML / OIDC) modes, SCIM behavior details (including rate limits and bulk endpoints), and the admin role model;
2) Sample logs/audit evidence export format and retention policy;
3) An estimate of delivery time for a demonstration environment if we request a proof-of-concept?

CC’ing Priya (Security) — she’ll coordinate follow-ups.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Initial RFI — technical details (SCIM / SSO / RBAC)

Tessa — quick technical notes below (copying what I’ll include in the capability pack). I can expand if CoreLedger wants a deep-dive call.

SAML / OIDC:
- Supported: SAML 2.0 (SP-initiated and IdP-initiated), OIDC 1.0 with standard auth code flow and PKCE.
- SAML attributes: configurable attribute mapping (email, external_id, groups, custom attributes). Assertions signed (SHA-256); metadata import supported.
- OIDC: standard OIDC claims supported; dynamic client registration is supported for private deployments via an admin API.
- Session management: token revocation and single logout (SLO) supported for SAML; OIDC sessions support RP-initiated logout and token introspection endpoints.

SCIM v2 behaviour:
- Endpoints: /scim/v2/Users and /scim/v2/Groups. Bulk support: POST /scim/v2/Bulk for batch create/update/delete (transactional semantics per request).
- Delta sync: supports sync tokens (since=) and incremental query using /Users?startIndex= and the returned "itemsPerPage"/"totalResults" headers for pagination. We provide a delta token in the response header X-Redwood-Delta for efficient polling.
- Group membership: group members are represented on the Group resource and via user.memberships; both canonicalized during import to avoid duplicates.
- Error handling: per-item error payloads for bulk endpoints; 429 with Retry-After when rate limits are hit. Default rate limits configurable for Dedicated/Private customers.
- SCIM throughput & limits: default hosted rate limit: 500 req/min for /Users (burstable with dedicated pools). Bulk requests are rate-limited by object count (default 2k members per bulk request).

RBAC / delegated admin model:
- Role model: three built-in roles (Organization Admin, Identity Admin, Read-only Auditor) and custom role creation scoped to tenant.
- Delegation: delegated admin scopes can be constrained to: product routes (e.g., embeddings only), specific model groups, or organizational units (OU).
- JIT access: supports just-in-time role elevation via OAuth/OIDC workflow and approval webhooks; can integrate with external approval systems (e.g., Jira, ServiceNow).
- Audit provenance: every admin action logs actor_id, session_id, IP, and a request_checksum; logs are tamper-evident (HMAC with KMS-managed key) and exportable via the Console or the Audit API.

Encryption & key management:
- Customer-managed keys: supported via KMS (GCP/AWS/Azure) and HSM options for Private deployments.

Retention & evidence exports:
- Audit log retention: default hosted retention 12 months; extendable to 36 months for Enterprise. Exports available in JSONL and NDJSON; compressed archives delivered over SFTP or via presigned URL to your storage.

Known caveats / notes:
- SCIM delta tokens are strong for incremental updates but require a monotonic sequence — bulk operations may produce out-of-order events which are reconciled during the next full sync.
- For very large directories we recommend a one-time snapshot import followed by delta sync for day-to-day operations.

I’ll drop the above into the PDF and include example payloads.
